name: the renderer's own path in the files it writes
why: The provenance text names the program that wrote the file: the managed-by header of permissions.yaml ("source: <floor> via <renderer>"), the "_" field of kiro-permissions-owned.json and the stamp key of the admin managed-settings.json. The original wrote global/kiro/kiro_permissions.py, which this slice deletes; the Node renderer writes src/render/kiro-permissions.js. The stamp, the floor source and every rule are still compared. Consequence on an installed machine: install-managed.sh --check reports the Kiro admin copy as DRIFT (not only STAMP) until the next --apply, and an existing permissions.yaml keeps the old header until a later install rewrites it; neither changes a rule.

name: the program name in the usage lines
why: The usage lines on stderr name the program: kiro_permissions.py in the original, kiro-permissions.js in the Node renderer. The rest of each usage line and the exit code 2 are still compared.

name: the way to remove a Kiro admin file Kiro rejects
pattern: sudo /bin/sh global/install-managed\.sh --remove|mhw install-admin --uninstall and the sudo line it prints
why: #496 (S26 of #470) deleted global/install-managed.sh: the FLOOR report for an admin Kiro file that is unreadable or that Kiro would reject told the owner to remove it with 'sudo /bin/sh global/install-managed.sh --remove', a command that no longer exists. It now names `mhw install-admin --uninstall and the sudo line it prints`, the admin layer's removal since #496. The rest of the line, 'or delete that one file as root' included, is compared unchanged.
